howDoI.q: How do I make a lever my hero can pull?
How do I make two levers add up to one bridge?
How do I send my hero back to the start without hurting them?
How do I make a trap door that opens when a lever is pulled?
How do I make a lever that is not for the bridge?
How do I wire a whole small puzzle out of counters?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Wired Room is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Up and Down climb a ladder. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Walk into a lever to pull it. Nothing in this game hurts: a pool or a hatch only sends you back to where you came in.

This one puts ideas from other Starters together in one room. Switches shows a lever filling a counter, and Both Together shows how a count stands in for an AND. Game-Maker has no AND or OR of its own: counters that add up do the same job.

pages.head: Level 1: Two Levers
pages.html:
Level 1: Two Levers

Three signs stand along the way. EACH LEVER ADDS 3 PLANKS comes first, then a red lever on the path. After a ladder up to a ledge with a second red lever come THE BRIDGE NEEDS 6 PLANKS and A SOFT POOL: YOU JUST START OVER, just before a pool with six dotted planks over it.

One lever builds only three planks. Walk out onto the planks with just that one and the first three turn solid, the fourth is not there, and you drop into the pool. It is soft. You start again at the way in with every life. Pull both levers and the whole bridge is yours.

There are twelve coins, worth ten points each, six of them over the planks.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • Two levers, one counter. Open pr.bbl in the blocks editor and pick leverRed. On its Touch tab, Effect counter is counter 22 and Effect amount is 3, and Becomes block is leverRedOn, the lever leaning the other way. Both levers in the level are this same block. Each pull puts 3 on counter 22.
  • Why there is no AND. A bridge cannot ask if both levers are pulled. Each dotted plank only takes one off counter 22. Six planks need six, and 3 + 3 is six. Pull just one and the counter runs out after three planks. Add up the counts and the bridge wants the sum.
  • The dotted plank. Pick ghostRed. Its Effect counter is 22 and its Effect amount is −1, and Becomes block is plank. A counter from 20 up will not go to zero or less, so with nothing on the counter the plank stays a dotted outline and you fall through it.
  • The soft pool. poolTop and pool take no hit points. Open one.map and look under the bridge. At the bottom of each pool square is a scene link. Open pr.gam and find the scene's links: each one points back at this same scene, at the entrance. A link sends the hero to its other end when they touch its first square, so a fall that touches the link is not a lost life.
  • The ledge. The second lever stands on a ledge of grass over dirt with a ladder up to it. A lever that takes some effort to reach feels like a reward.
  • The counter itself. Open hero.chr in the character editor. Counter 22 starts at 1, which the game shows as none.

pages.head: Level 2: Wired Room
pages.html:
Level 2: Wired Room

A taller sign, BLUE LEVERS BUILD THE BRIDGE, comes first, then a blue lever on the path. ONE BLUE LEVER IS UP THE LADDER points at a ledge. Up there are a second blue lever, a sign that says RED LEVER OPENS THE HATCH and an odd red lever at the end. Past it, A HATCH IN THE PATH stands before a red-framed trap door in the ground, and 6 PLANKS NEED BOTH BLUE LEVERS stands before a pool with six blue dotted planks.

The two blue levers build the bridge, as in level 1. The red lever has nothing to do with the bridge: it puts two on a counter that only the hatch spends. Pull it and walk on, and the hatch opens under you and drops you into a hole, which sends you back to the way in with every life. Leave it alone and the hatch stays shut, so you walk right over it.

There are ten coins, worth ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Three counters in all. Level 1 used 22. Here the blue levers and the blue planks use counter 23 and the red lever and the hatch use counter 24. Counters carry over from one level to the next, which is why this level does not reuse 22. Open leverBlue, ghostBlue, leverHatch and hatch and compare their Effect counter numbers.
  • The hatch. Pick hatch. It is solid, so you walk on it. Its Effect counter is 24 and its Effect amount is −1, and Becomes block is hatchOpen, a hole in the same square. With counter 24 empty the touch is refused and it stays shut. It is two squares wide: if it were one, you could walk across before you fell. Each square spends one, so the red lever (leverHatch) puts two on counter 24.
  • The hole. cave is a dark hole under each hatch square, with a scene link at the bottom, just like the pool. Open two.map in the map editor and look under the hatch.
  • Nothing is joined. The blue levers, the red lever, the planks and the hatch never talk to each other. Counters 23 and 24 are all that connect them, so the red lever cannot build the bridge and the blue levers cannot open the hatch.
  • Starting over. A link into the same scene starts the room again, and counters keep their numbers. Pull a blue lever again and its count adds on top of what is left, so a few planks are saved up after a fall.
  • The signs and the exit. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. The last door links to the The End scene in pr.gam.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Change leverBlue's Effect amount to 6, and see that one lever builds the whole bridge.
  • Change the Effect counter of leverHatch to 23, and see what the red lever builds.
  • Change leverHatch's Effect amount to 1, and see what the hatch does when only one square is paid for.
  • Redraw ghostBlue in the blocks editor so the unbuilt bridge looks like something else.
  • Add a third blue lever to two.map and a longer bridge, so every lever counts.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.back: A small explorer in a blue beanie finds a bridge of dotted planks and a few levers. Two levers add up to a whole bridge, and a third is wired to a trap door that only drops you back to the start. Nothing is hurt, nothing is lost, and every lever works through counters you can change. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and rewire it.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
Levers fill counters and planks and a hatch spend them
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Two short levels about putting counters together. Lian finds levers, a bridge of dotted planks and a pool that is only soft. Each lever puts planks on a counter, and each plank spends one, so two levers build a bridge neither can alone. In the second room one lever is wired to a hatch in the path instead, and pulling it drops Lian back to the start with nothing hurt. Signs say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and rewire a lever.

57.long: Jump. Steer with Left and Right while you are in the air.

counters.20: Keys: not used here, but a copy can add them.
counters.22: Level 1 planks: each red lever adds 3, each red plank takes one.
counters.23: Level 2 planks: each blue lever adds 3, each blue plank takes one.
counters.24: Hatch: the red lever adds 2, each hatch square takes one.
